issue_context.title: TarEntry: link target path checks
issue_context.body:
@carlossanlop @Jozkee do we need these checks:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ea4f2cc6190b1fbcc53e27e9b21a91eeea5b7736/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/src/System/Formats/Tar/TarEntry.cs#L504-L523

I'm not sure what the `Path.Exists` is about?

For the hard link, it seems they check conditions on which creating the hard link will fail. So we might just as well fail when the link gets created.

If we can get rid of the checks, we can simplify the code a little because there is no need to pass around `linkTargetPath` to this method.

I tried leaving them out, and there were no test failures.

Huh actually this keeps failing with IOException on the Symlink case.

I looked at the tar change history. I remember we introduced this removed code section as a preventative measure. Here is the commit: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/67883/commits/5d815778eb5ea9c4a2fda774472c40b824c0bf02

The commit name is "Disallow extracting individual links". The limitation prevents someone from using the TarFile APIs  to point to a file that does not yet exist.

I'd be happy to revisit this. The removed code has two parts:

A) Prevent extracting a symlink whose target does not yet exist.
B) Prevent extracting a hardlink whose target does not yet exist, or attempting to create a hardlink that points to a directory.

@GrabYourPitchforks - Do you think these checks could be removed so TarFile is not so restricted? Notice @tmds added a new test to confirm that a symlink can be extracted when the target does not yet exist.

> A) Prevent extracting a symlink whose target does not yet exist

Tar writers don't guarantee that symbolic link targets are in the archive before the symbolic links, which is what this code was assuming.

> B) Prevent extracting a hardlink whose target does not yet exist, or attempting to create a hardlink that points to a directory.

hardlinks can never be created to targets that don't exist, or to a directory.
Note that this does **not** change the restriction that link targets must point in the destination directory.
It may be fine to drop the "target does not yet exist" validation for symbolic links. `File.CreateSymbolicLink` does not enforce that the target exists so I think is fine to align the behavior here.
Yes, they can be dropped. I'll include a comment explaining why.
How can we assume that LinkName will never be an absolute path for hard links?
We're using `Path.Join` to interpret the `LinkName` as a relative path.

Someone could use a `TarWriter` to manually write a Hard Link entry with LinkName = "C:\my\absolute\path". I don't think is something worth validating because likely no tools would produce it but is something to have in mind.
What do we do if the hard link target does not exist at the moment of extraction i.e: on `CreateNonRegularFile`? I expect that the respective syscall fails.

Yes it fails, and that is the proper thing to do.
Hard links are detected and handled by the tar writer. It won't include a hard link before the target file.

note: .NET's tar writer doesn't detect hard links and treats them like regular files. There is an open issue to handle them: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/74404.

These checks are removed from this function:

- The `targetDirectoryPath` checks the directory of the target exists when the entry is extracted. There is no reason we must require the directory to exist. And, the directory could still be created later.
- The checks when `!string.IsNullOrEmpty(linkTargetPath)` for `HardLink` check things that will cause the hard link creation to fail, so there's no need to verify them.
- `string.IsNullOrEmpty(linkTargetPath)` cannot happen from the callers of this function.

Thanks for the change, and sorry for the lack of answer in the initial issue.

> And, the directory could still be created later.

Do you mind adding tests that extract links pointing to non-existent files and directories? For the TarEntry and the TarFile extract methods, sync and async.

Actually, please hold on. I'm currently looking at the code's history. There are many security protections we decided to add, which restrict the functionality of TarFile.ExtractToDirectory and TarEntry.ExtractToFile by design.

> The targetDirectoryPath checks the directory of the target exists when the entry is extracted. There is no reason we must require the directory to exist. And, the directory could still be created later.

I've added a test for this.
